Gradient curve

Flow is not a tap — it is a gradient. Choose how quickly outward flow ramps up as your balance moves from floor toward ceiling.

Generous early
Start flowing at ~20% above floor; full output near ceiling
Linear
Even ramp from floor to ceiling; equal proportion at each point
Cautious
Hold most back until close to abundance; surge near ceiling
Almost everyone is always flowing something. The gradient model means you give a little while still receiving a little — that simultaneous give-and-receive is what keeps the web alive.
Anti-hoarding mechanisms
Gradient outflow Live
Surplus above ceiling flows out automatically through your trust channels toward need. The gradient curve above governs the ramp.
Activity-decay Live
Flow entitlement diminishes as a contributor becomes inactive — they "drift from the river." Does not reduce the recipient's actual balance; it reduces future flow allocation to them.
Decay starts after reaching zero after
Demurrage — balance decay Simulation only
Idle balances lose a small % per period, incentivising circulation. Live tension: may push toward external investment rather than circulation. Enabled here for simulation only — run the simulation surface to explore the effect on your specific network before arming live.
